Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

attinet

attinet (ad)

verb: third person of attineō, with ad and the accusative

it concerns, it has to do with

In this lexicon

  • concern

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Trin. 1065: quid id ad mē attinet?; Traupman 294

  • nihil ad tē attinet: business

    classical

  • quod ad … attinet: respect

    classical

Examples

  • quid id ad mē attinet?

    what has that to do with me?Plaut. Trin. 1065

    In the entry for concern

  • Istae quid ad mē? — Immō ad tē attinent et tuā rēfert.

    What have these to do with me? — Oh, they concern you, and it matters to you.Plaut. Pers. 497

    In the entry for concern

  • tantumne est ab rē tuā ōtī tibi, aliēna ut cūrēs eaque nihil quae ad tē attinent?

    have you so much time to spare from your own affairs that you look after other people’s, which don’t concern you?Ter. Heaut. 75–76 (Parry’s text)

    In the entry for concern

  • nam tua rēs agitur, pariēs cum proximus ārdet

    for it is your concern when the wall next door is on fireHor. Ep. 1.18.84

    In the entry for concern
